name: Coordinate Geometry: From Zero
competency: Cartesian plane representation, linear equations y = mx + c, slope as rate of change, point of intersection in systems of linear equations, and budget inequalities modeled through 4 real-life stories
ncertStandard: NCERT Class 9 Chapter 3 (Coordinate Geometry), Class 9 Chapter 4 (Linear Equations in Two Variables), and Class 10 Chapter 3 (Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables)
overview: A unified story-driven learning module that takes students from zero to mastery in coordinate geometry. Spans four interconnected real-life scenarios: (1) Classroom fish market seating grid & collinearity, (2) Rahul's night-before exam rate optimization and sleep strategy, (3) Raju Kirana robbery mystery solved via intersection of linear equations, and (4) School canteen samosa party cost function and budget constraints.
learningOutcomes: Identify Cartesian coordinate components: Origin (0,0), X-axis (rows), and Y-axis (seats)
Plot ordered pairs (x, y) on a GeoGebra-style interactive coordinate plane
Discover collinearity and write linear relations (y = 2x + 3) connecting plotted points
Interpret slope (m) as rate of change (questions per hour) and y-intercept (c) as initial condition in y = mx + c
Solve simultaneous linear equations graphically by pinpointing their unique intersection point (4, 0)
Formulate linear cost functions C(x) = 12x + 20 and evaluate linear budget inequalities (12x + 20 <= 200)

levels.name: Story 1: Classroom Ka Fish Market
levels.description: Plot Parth & Anish from Origin (0,0) and determine Amit's seat on the straight line

levels.name: Story 2: Rahul Ki Night-Before Strategy
levels.description: Model exam preparation rate y = mx + c to finish 40 questions and maximize sleep

levels.name: Story 3: Raju Kirana Robbery Mystery
levels.description: Graph 3 daily store receipts and identify the intersection point (4, 0) to catch the thief

levels.name: Story 4: Canteen Ki Samosa Party
levels.description: Model party expense function C(x) = 12x + 20 and solve 12x + 20 <= 200 budget constraint
